Consider the finite region $D$ in the $xy$-plane enclosed by the lines $y=-x,$ $y=x+4,$ $y=0$ and $y=4,$ as shown in the picture. Express the double integral of the function $f(x,y)$ over the region $D$ as a sum of repeated integrals over type II regions.
question.worked_solution:
First, let's write our equations in terms of $y,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}y=-x & \,⟹\,x=-y \\ y=x+4 & \,⟹\,x=y-4\end{aligned}
$$

The region $D$ can be partitioned into two type II regions ${D}_{1}$ and ${D}_{2},$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14153479/assets/17d3ceabf3cd7a052398d8d12b7963c5ca64356605554e3ff43c21c7321e45de.png)

  

As a result, we get

$$
{D}_{1}=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 2,\,y-4\le x\le -y\}
$$

and 

$$
{D}_{2}=\{(x,y)\,:\,2\le y\le 4,\,-y\le x\le y-4\}.
$$

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA & ={∬}_{{D}_{1}}f(x,y)\,dA+{∬}_{{D}_{2}}f(x,y)\,dA \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{y-4}^{-y}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{2}^{4}{\int }_{-y}^{y-4}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$
